tonight.headline: The trade you have now sent six times is priced with the wrong player. Offer Tuten, not Golden - it is worth three times as much to Team 13 and costs you nothing this week.
body: Dead even again: ESPN has you 119.6 to KEI returns' 117.8 at 51%, nothing has kicked off, and your first lock is Sunday 11:00 Mexico City.

Two things are still undone from yesterday. Trevor Lawrence is still in your starting slot - the swap to Matthew Stafford was recommended at 07:55 and has not been made, and the condition behind it is unchanged: FantasyPros have the Giants 22nd of 32 and Denver 8th. And the Team 13 quarterback offer is still unanswered after six sends.

The new thing is why it is unanswered. I re-ran the full one-for-one search over both rosters on this morning's snapshot and the Golden version gives Team 13 +12.2. The same trade with Bhayshul Tuten as the chip gives them +40.6 - more than three times as much - and still gains you +11.6. It also leaves Golden in your flex, and Golden is the better Week 2 start by a distance. Send the Tuten version.

case.label: Why the chip was wrong
case.body: Team 13's flex is Travis Kelce at 178.1, so Golden at 190.3 upgrades them by 12.2. But their second running back is Rachaad White at 164.6, and Tuten at 205.2 upgrades that slot by 40.6. Six briefs have been pricing this trade from your side of the ledger only. Their hole is at running back, not at flex, and the offer has been aimed at the wrong hole the whole time.

case.label: Why it costs you nothing you will feel
case.body: On a season view Golden is the better chip for you - giving him is +26.5 against Tuten's +11.6 - because Tuten is currently your optimal flex at 205.2 to Golden's 190.3. On this week it inverts completely: Golden faces the Jets, 31st of 32, and Tuten faces Denver at 8th with no goal-line role. And if the Furia Regia trade below also lands, McLaurin takes the flex and the two versions end in exactly the same place, 2115.4 either way. I recomputed that; it is not an estimate.

case.label: Their softest point, unchanged
case.body: KEI returns start Jaxson Dart with Patrick Mahomes at 17.3 on their bench, which is still the strangest thing in this league. They also spent priority on Jalen Coker at 07:09 and he sits behind Drake London and George Pickens. Their week rests on De'Von Achane at San Francisco, 4th of 32, with Malik Willis at quarterback in a declared Miami rebuild.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 trade or drop a quarterback, or acquire a running back - either kills the +40.6 that makes this version work. Also falsified if Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report, which I could not check: every Lamar injury page retrievable this run was from 2025.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Lamar Jackson locks Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Send Team 13 a new offer: Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson
doFirst.subtitle: Replaces the Golden version, which has gone unanswered six times. Same player back, a chip worth 3.3x more to them: +11.6 you, +40.6 them.

case.label: Why they say yes to this and not the last one
case.body: I checked their slot column on this morning's file, not a carried note: Josh Allen is at slot 0 and starting, Lamar Jackson is at slot 20 on the bench, and Lamar is not being asked to give up a starter. Their weakest starting slot is the second running back, Rachaad White at 164.6 season behind Christian McCaffrey. Tuten at 205.2 goes straight into it for +40.6. Golden only ever upgraded their flex off Travis Kelce for +12.2, which is inside the range a manager ignores.

case.label: Why you say yes
case.body: Lamar Jackson at 312.9 becomes your starting quarterback over Stafford at 286.4. Tuten leaving drops your flex from 205.2 to Golden's 190.3, so the net is +11.6 rather than +26.5 - a smaller number than the Golden version and a far likelier one to be accepted. You are also selling the asset whose role Draft Sharks just described as capped: 15 carries but Chris Rodriguez Jr. took the only goal-line snap and five of eight short-yardage plays, and out-ran him on routes.

case.label: What it does to this Sunday
case.body: It improves it. Golden stays in your flex facing the Jets at 31st of 32 after a team-high 12 targets on 40 routes in Week 1; Tuten would have been in your flex facing Denver at 8th with no red-zone work. The Golden version of this trade was explicitly a season-horizon play that cost you the week. This one does not.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, which removes the hole Tuten fills; or they trade or drop a quarterback, which removes the surplus. Also falsified if Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report - nothing on his 2026 health was retrievable this run and the price rests entirely on a seasonProj field that has now been identical for seven consecutive snapshots. Read +11.6 as a direction, not a decimal.

doFirst.title: Start Matthew Stafford, bench Trevor Lawrence - still not done
doFirst.subtitle: Recommended at 07:55 this morning and not executed. Lawrence is still in slot 0 on this snapshot. The condition that fired has not unfired.

case.label: The clause that fired, re-verified today
case.body: Monday's hold wrote its own falsification: a Week 2 read placing the Giants defense outside the top 20 flips this to Stafford. I retrieved FantasyPros' Week 2 board myself this run rather than carrying yesterday's citation - the Giants are 22nd of 32 and Denver is 8th. Lawrence faces the harder defence by fourteen places. Jacksonville's implied total at 21.0 did not fall below 19, so this flips on one condition and not both, which is worth saying plainly.

case.label: Where projection and reporting agree
case.body: ESPN project Stafford 17.4 and Lawrence 14.8, and the matchup board points the same way, which is unusual enough to note. The original Lawrence hold rested on one box score - 18 of 23 for 245 and four touchdowns - and the standing rule is that Weeks 1 to 3 are noise and role is what matters. Lawrence's role has not changed; his draw has.

case.label: What I could not check, and it matters here
case.body: Stafford's own falsification clause was 'appears on the Rams injury report'. I could not test it. Every Matthew Stafford injury result retrievable this run was from 2025 - an August 2025 back-injury page about a preseason Chargers game, a 2025 concussion protocol piece, a divisional-round finger sprain. There is no current Rams reporting in this decision at all, and Stafford has a documented back history. If he shows up limited on Wednesday, this card is void and Lawrence starts.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Stafford appears on any Rams injury report, Lawrence out-scores him on Sunday, or the Team 13 trade lands - which retires the question by putting Lamar Jackson in the slot and both of these men on the bench.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Jacksonville kick off Sunday 14:05 Mexico City
doFirst.title: New: offer Furia Regia Trevor Lawrence for Terry McLaurin
doFirst.subtitle: Sells the quarterback you are about to bench anyway. +13.1 you, +3.7 them - but you are asking for a starter, so read the odds honestly.

case.label: Why this exists
case.body: You carry two quarterbacks in a one-quarterback league. The moment you bench Lawrence for Stafford, Lawrence is worth exactly zero to you every week - the same structural waste this brief has spent six runs pointing out on Team 13's roster. Furia Regia start Justin Herbert at 271.0; Lawrence at 282.0 upgrades them by 11.0 at the position that matters most.

case.label: Your side
case.body: McLaurin at 218.3 takes your flex off Tuten at 205.2 for +13.1, and if the Team 13 trade also lands, McLaurin takes it off Golden at 190.3 instead - the two deals compose to +39.6 rather than colliding. That is the recomputed number on full rosters ignoring this week's kickoffs, per the trade rules.

case.label: The honest problem with the odds
case.body: Terry McLaurin is at slot 23 - their flex - which is a starting slot, not a bench seat. You are asking a 1-0 team to give up a starter, which is a different conversation from asking Team 13 for a benched quarterback. Their net is only +3.7 because Swift at 211.0 backfills the flex. Call it a longshot and send it anyway, because the downside is a declined message.

case.label: What I could not check
case.body: McLaurin himself. Every 2026 search for him returned 2025 pages, including one saying he and Jayden Daniels were both out against Atlanta - that is last season. I have no current usage, target share or health information on the player you would be acquiring. That is a real hole in a trade recommendation and it is why this is SOLID rather than ELITE.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin appears on Washington's Wednesday injury report, Furia Regia acquire a quarterback, or Jayden Daniels is ruled out - any of which changes what you are buying. Also retire it if the Team 13 deal lands and you would rather not carry three quarterbacks' worth of trade conversations at once.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only - fire it after today's Raiders report, not before
doFirst.title: If Bowers practises in full today: add T.J. Hockenson, drop Michael Mayer
doFirst.subtitle: Third consecutive run parked on a practice report. It is now Wednesday morning Eastern - the report lands this afternoon and you can act on it yourself.

case.label: The trigger, written on 14 September
case.body: 'Bowers practises in full Wednesday or carries no designation Friday - then drop Mayer before week 2. Bowers is limited or sits out Wednesday - then keep Mayer through week 2.' Today is that Wednesday and the session has not happened at the time of writing.

case.label: What is known as of this morning
case.body: New detail this run: DraftKings Network have the meniscus procedure dated 9 September, Bowers originally expected to miss one to two games, currently day-to-day, with coach Kubiak indicating flexibility on his availability. ESPN carry him QUESTIONABLE at 14.4 projected. That is a club expecting him to play, which is the direction that ends Mayer's role. Note that a widely-circulating CBS piece describing Bowers under Pete Carroll is from September 2025 and is about a different injury; I discarded it.

case.label: Why Hockenson and why it costs nothing
case.body: He is a free agent here at 61.8% rostered - the ownership anomaly that means a manager blundered, and it costs no waiver priority, which is the entire point in a league where priority never resets and you are sitting on an unspent 3rd of 10. He ran 81% of Minnesota's routes for a 16% target share as the second option behind Justin Jefferson. IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so Hockenson at 158.9 is a real flex alternative; Mayer at 85.0 is not.

case.label: The churn rule, which nobody has applied to this card
case.body: STRATEGY.md section 3 closes any roster spot that changed hands in the last seven days unless a player in it is ruled out. Mayer arrived on 10 September, so this seat is six days old and technically still inside that window until tomorrow. What lets the card stand is the same section's other clause: a seat opens when the thesis visibly breaks, and the Mayer thesis wrote its own expiry - Bowers returning. If Bowers is full today the thesis has broken and the move is inside policy; if he is limited, the seat is closed on both counts.

case.label: The quarterback caveat on both of them
case.body: Hockenson's quarterback is unsettled - Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and highly questionable, with sources split between Carson Wentz and Cam Ward as the replacement. Mayer's is Kirk Cousins per the league file's roster mapping, which I did not verify with reporting. Neither tight end here has a settled passer and you should not expect either to be a weekly starter.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bowers limited or absent from today's session, or carrying a designation on Friday - then keep Mayer through Week 2 exactly as 14 September decided. Also void if Hockenson is rostered before you act.

whatWentWrong.title: Six runs have sent Team 13 the wrong half of a good idea. The trade was right; the chip was wrong.
whatWentWrong.lead: Golden for Lamar gives them +12.2. Tuten for Lamar gives them +40.6 and still gains you +11.6. Nobody had checked which of their slots was actually leaking.

case.label: The error
case.body: Every previous run priced this deal by asking what Hans gains and then checking that the other side was not negative. +12.2 clears that test. But Team 13's flex is Travis Kelce at 178.1, which is a survivable slot, while their second running back is Rachaad White at 164.6 behind Christian McCaffrey, which is a hole. The offer was aimed at the slot that was not bleeding.

case.label: Why it went unnoticed six times
case.body: Because the exhaustive pair search was run and the top result by your own gain was taken as the answer. Sorted by your gain, Golden-for-Lamar is first at +26.5 and Tuten-for-Lamar is fourth at +11.6. Sorted by their gain, the order reverses. A trade that is never accepted is worth zero, so the ranking that matters is theirs.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: Six days of a 0-1 team not having the second-best quarterback in the league. It is not recoverable and it is worth logging plainly rather than presenting today's version as a discovery.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 decline the Tuten version too, which would mean the objection was never about price and the whole read on that manager is wrong. If both versions are declined by Friday, stop sending and say so here.

whatWentWrong.title: Colston Loveland's Week 1 zero is worse than yesterday's brief said, and yesterday's brief had a fact backwards.
whatWentWrong.lead: Chicago scored 59 points. He caught nothing. And Cole Kmet - the tight end the brief said Loveland was taking third downs from - caught a 22-yard touchdown in double coverage.

case.label: What was actually reported
case.body: Pro Football Network, 13 September: in a 59-37 win over Carolina, Loveland was targeted twice and caught none of them while leading the team in routes run. The rest of the offence produced 552 yards. D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai dominated the target share out of the backfield, and Kmet scored.

case.label: Why it changes the read
case.body: Yesterday's tile called the zero noise and the usage real, on the argument that he ran 100% of third-down snaps over Kmet. Route share in a blowout is the cheapest usage statistic there is - the routes came, the ball did not, in a game where the offence could not stop scoring. A tight end who cannot get targeted in a 59-point game has a targeting problem, not a snap problem. Ben Johnson is quoted wanting to address it, which is an admission that it is a problem.

case.label: What it does not change
case.body: He is still your tight end. He is the TE3 by analyst rank at 207.2 season, Minnesota are 21st of 32, and the alternative is Michael Mayer at 85.0. This is a downgrade in confidence, not a lineup change - and it is the reason Hockenson is a genuine flex consideration rather than a throwaway fallback.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Fewer than four targets again on Sunday. Two weeks of that against Carolina and Minnesota is a role problem and no matchup grade survives it.

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup change this brief called ELITE at 07:55 has not been made, five hours later.
whatWentWrong.lead: Trevor Lawrence is still in slot 0 on the 12:52 snapshot. Matthew Stafford is still on the bench. Nothing in the file suggests the swap was attempted.

case.label: The state of play
case.body: Your last lineup activity in this league was at 17:50 on 15 September - Tuten and Golden - and before that 07:18 on 15 September for Stafford and Lawrence, which is the move that put Lawrence in. Yesterday's 07:55 brief reversed that call. The activity log shows no lineup change since.

case.label: Why it is being repeated rather than assumed
case.body: Because the app shows what this file contains, and dropping the card on the assumption it had been actioned would have removed the only lineup instruction in the league. The runbook's own rule is to check the slot column before recommending a change; the slot column says the change has not happened.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Making the swap in ESPN, or Stafford appearing on a Rams injury report - which, as the card says, I could not check this run at all.

case.label: Their structural surplus, verified today
case.body: Josh Allen at slot 0 and Lamar Jackson at slot 20 in a one-quarterback league, checked against the 12:52 snapshot rather than carried. Allen is starting and is not being asked for. One of their two best assets scores them zero every week.

case.body: Not the flex. Travis Kelce at 178.1 in the flex is survivable. Rachaad White at 164.6 as the starting RB2 behind McCaffrey is not. Tuten upgrades that by 40.6 where Golden upgraded the flex by 12.2.

case.body: Lamar at 312.9 replaces Stafford at 286.4 at quarterback for +26.5; losing Tuten drops the flex from 205.2 to Golden at 190.3 for -14.9; net +11.6. trades.headline: You are about to bench a 282-point quarterback for good. Sell him to the team whose starter he beats.

case.label: Why it is available at all
case.body: Furia Regia start Justin Herbert at 271.0. Lawrence at 282.0 is an upgrade at the one position they cannot double up on. They are deep at receiver - CeeDee Lamb and Justin Jefferson are their starters - which is why McLaurin is the flex and why he is the piece that can move.

case.label: Your side, and how it composes
case.body: McLaurin at 218.3 takes the flex off Tuten at 205.2 for +13.1. If the Team 13 deal also lands, McLaurin takes the flex off Golden at 190.3 and the two together are +39.6. They do not collide, which is the point of running the search over full rosters rather than one deal at a time.

case.label: The reason this is a longshot and not an even offer
case.body: Slot 23 is their flex, which starts. Asking a 1-0 team for a starter to fix your quarterback redundancy is a harder sell than asking a 0-1 team for a benched quarterback, and +3.7 is inside the range a manager declines without replying. Send it, expect nothing, and do not send it twice.

case.label: What I could not check
case.body: Anything at all about Terry McLaurin in 2026. Every search returned 2025 pages, one of which said he and Jayden Daniels were both out against Atlanta - that is last season and it is not current. You would be acquiring a player on a projection field and a matchup rank alone.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin appears on Washington's Wednesday report, Furia Regia acquire a quarterback, or Jayden Daniels is ruled out.

worthALook.lead: Free here at 61.8% rostered, and promoted from fallback to genuine flex candidate by what Colston Loveland did not do in Week 1.

case.label: Why the case got stronger today
case.body: It is no longer only about Michael Mayer's seat expiring. Loveland caught nothing on two targets while Chicago scored 59 points, which makes Hockenson a real alternative rather than a bench swap. IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so he can start for you without displacing Loveland at all.

case.label: The role
case.body: 81% of Minnesota's routes for a 16% target share and a touchdown in Week 1, second target behind Justin Jefferson. That is the usage profile Loveland was credited with and did not convert.

case.label: The problem you should weigh
case.body: His quarterback. Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and called highly questionable, and the sources disagree about whether Carson Wentz or Cam Ward replaces him. Adding a tight end for his target share and then handing him a third-string passer is the failure mode worth naming out loud.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Today, after the Raiders practice report, if Bowers is full - the doFirst card above is armed for exactly that. Independently of Bowers, act if Loveland draws fewer than four targets on Sunday. He is a free agent, so this costs no priority either way.

worthALook.name: Jordan Mason
worthALook.lead: Declined for the fifth run and recorded again so no future run rediscovers him - but the QUESTIONABLE tag finally has a cause behind it.

case.label: What is new
case.body: The tag that three previous briefs could not explain is thumb soreness, picked up in Minnesota's Week 1 win, per DraftKings Network on 15 September. He is being evaluated. That closes an open unknown rather than leaving it hanging.

case.label: What kills it, unchanged
case.body: He would not start. Your backs are Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley and the flex is a live question between Golden, Tuten and potentially McLaurin. DraftKings also correct the earlier read: Mason split snaps nearly equally with Aaron Jones rather than leading the backfield. Carries without targets is the least valuable shape in full PPR.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Taylor or Barkley missing time. He is a free agent now, not a claim, so the priority objection is gone and only the 'he would not start' argument remains - which means any injury to your top two makes him immediately worth a seat.

doNotChase.name: Josh Allen
doNotChase.lead: The trade search says asking Team 13 for Josh Allen gains you +16.9 and gains them +21.8. Do not send it.

case.label: Why the maths says yes
case.body: Garrett Wilson for Josh Allen: Allen at 366.5 replaces Stafford at 286.4, Wilson at 253.5 leaves and Golden backfills. Their side works because Lamar at 312.9 simply slides into the slot Allen vacates and Wilson at 253.5 upgrades their flex off Kelce at 178.1. On a spreadsheet it is the largest mutual-gain pair in the league.

case.label: Why you still do not send it
case.body: Allen is at slot 0. He is their starting quarterback and the consensus QB1 overall. No manager reads an offer for their starting QB1 as anything other than a lowball, whatever the numbers underneath say, and sending it burns the credibility you need for the Lamar offer that is actually live. The rule is that you ask for the benched asset, not the started one.

case.label: The rule this is already covered by
case.body: STRATEGY.md section 7 carries a standing default: any player who is top-5 at his position is untouchable regardless of the math, and it names this exact failure - 'the optimiser will occasionally propose trading an elite quarterback for a flex receiver because a backup appears to backfill the slot. It is always wrong.' Josh Allen is the consensus QB1. The pair search surfaced precisely the trade that rule was written to stop, which is a point in favour of the rule rather than the search.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 accepting the Lamar deal first, which would leave Allen as their only quarterback and make him untouchable anyway - or Team 13 opening the conversation themselves. Recorded here so the next run does not present it as a discovery.

doNotChase.lead: The weekly kicker comparison, and the answer is hold Cam Little for the fifth run running.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 board has Cam Little K3. The best available here is Will Reichard at K5, then Chase McLaughlin K6, Trey Smack K13, Cairo Santos K14, Evan McPherson K15, Chris Boswell K17. Nothing on this wire beats what you own and the two kickers above Little are both rostered.

case.label: The caveat I am not hiding
case.body: Little kicks at Denver, 8th of 32, and ESPN price him 8.1 against Santos's 9.0. The rank and the weekly projection disagree. I take the rank because a kicker's rank is leg and volume and one matchup moves it little - but for this week in isolation Santos is the play. This is carried from yesterday; I ran no new kicker research this run.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Little finishing outside the top 20 kickers across Weeks 2 to 4. That clause is on the record from 14 September and is unchanged. The kicker seat has been churned twice in this league for no stated reason; leave it alone.

candidates.note: T.J. Hockenson, TE MIN, free at 61.8% rostered. 81% route share and a 16% target share as Minnesota's second option behind Jefferson. Promoted from Bowers-fallback to genuine flex candidate because Loveland caught nothing on two targets in a 59-point Chicago win. IPADE's flex takes a tight end so he starts without displacing Loveland. The catch is his quarterback: Kyler Murray is in concussion protocol and the replacement is disputed between Carson Wentz and Cam Ward.

Jordan Mason, RB MIN, free at 67.6% rostered. Declined for the fifth run. New this run: the unexplained QUESTIONABLE tag is thumb soreness from the Week 1 win, and DraftKings correct the earlier read - he split snaps nearly evenly with Aaron Jones rather than leading the backfield. Carries without targets is the weakest shape in full PPR. Act only if Taylor or Barkley miss time.

Romeo Doubs, WR NE, free at 59.7% rostered. A.J. Brown is on IR for six games, but New England's WR1 job is a live three-way argument between Doubs, Mack Hollins and DeMario Douglas, and SI describe Doubs as rebounding from a shaky debut. Yesterday's brief overstated him as the priority pickup. He would not start ahead of Rice, Wilson or Golden. Kayshon Boutte at 13.9% rostered is the seat if this ever changes.

settled.title: Offer Team 13 Matthew Golden for Lamar Jackson (11-16 September, six sends)
settled.result: Retired and replaced. The trade was right and the chip was wrong: Golden gives them +12.2 into a survivable flex, Tuten gives them +40.6 into a leaking RB2 slot. Recomputed on this morning's snapshot. Six runs priced the deal from your side only.

settled.title: Start Trevor Lawrence over Matthew Stafford (14 September, reversed 16 September)
settled.result: Still reversed and still not executed. Lawrence remains in slot 0 on the 12:52 snapshot. The Giants at 22nd and Denver at 8th were re-verified against a freshly retrieved FantasyPros board rather than carried from yesterday's citation.

settled.title: Call Colston Loveland's Week 1 zero noise on his route share (16 September)
settled.result: Too generous. Chicago scored 59 points and gained 552 yards while he caught nothing on two targets, and Cole Kmet - the tight end he was said to be taking third downs from - scored. Route share in a blowout is not evidence. He stays in the lineup because the alternative is Mayer at 85.0, not because the usage argument survived.

settled.title: Decline the Tampa Bay defense as a claim and wait for free agency (16 September)
settled.result: Confirmed by your own transaction. Los Cachanillas claimed Tampa Bay at 07:09, the conditional add went void, and you added Baltimore as a free agent at 07:24 for zero priority. Baltimore is 3rd of 32 this week against a New Orleans offence ranked 26th.

settled.title: Decline Jalen Coker as a claim here (15 September)
settled.result: Held and immediately vindicated. KEI returns spent priority on him at 07:09 and he sits on their bench behind Drake London and George Pickens. You kept your 3rd-of-10 priority and you own him in Chem for free.

settled.title: Start Matthew Golden in the flex over Bhayshul Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Executed Monday 17:50 and now doubly right. Golden: team-high 12 targets on 40 routes into a Jets defence ranked 31st. Draft Sharks confirm Tuten's cap - no goal line, fewer routes than Chris Rodriguez Jr. The tension is resolved today: Tuten is the trade chip and Golden stays.

settled.title: Add Michael Mayer for the Brock Bowers absence (10 September)
settled.result: Expiring, third run running. New detail: the meniscus trim was 9 September, Bowers was expected to miss one to two games and is day-to-day with the coach signalling flexibility. Today is the Wednesday the trigger was written for and the session has not happened yet.

settled.title: Hold Cam Little and compare him every week (14 September)
settled.result: Hold, fifth run. Little is K3 on PFN's Week 2 board; the best available is Reichard at K5. Carried without new research this run and flagged as such.

settled.title: Decline Bo Nix on the free-agent artifact (14 September)
settled.result: Holding, and about to matter more. You start one quarterback and carry two; if the Lamar deal lands you carry three until Lawrence moves. A fourth is the last thing this roster needs.

cannotSee.label: Nothing on Lamar Jackson or Matthew Stafford in 2026 was retrievable, and both trades and the lineup card rest on them
cannotSee.body: Every Lamar Jackson injury page that came back described a 2025 back contusion, a Saturday game against Green Bay and a fifth injury of that season. Every Stafford page was 2025 too - an August preseason back injury against the Chargers, a concussion protocol piece, a divisional-round finger sprain. Stafford's own falsification clause was 'appears on the Rams injury report' and I could not test it. These are the two most load-bearing unknowns in the file.

cannotSee.label: Terry McLaurin is in a trade recommendation and was never successfully researched
cannotSee.body: Every 2026 search returned 2025 pages, including one stating he and Jayden Daniels were both out against Atlanta. I have no current usage, target share or health information on him. The Furia Regia offer is priced on a seasonProj field and a matchup rank alone, which is why it is SOLID rather than ELITE.

Carson Wentz carries a season projection of 0.5 and a weekly projection of 15.5. Both trade prices - +11.6 and +13.1 - come out of that field. Read them as directions, not decimals.

The league file has Wentz on Minnesota and Cam Ward on Tennessee, so I took Wentz. T.J. Hockenson's value depends on which is right and I cannot settle it.

cannotSee.label: The matchup grades are one board, and for a D/ST that board is about the offence it faces
cannotSee.body: All tiles come from FantasyPros' Week 2 defense streaming board of 32, which ranks defences as fantasy plays. Yesterday's brief shipped an inversion off a board like this - reading Kansas City at 7th as a statement about the Colts defence. Every tile here is the rank of the defence the player faces, read in one direction, and the Rashee Rice correction holds on today's board at 28th.

cannotSee.label: The runbook contains a second, drifted validator that contradicts the repository's own
cannotSee.body: The runbook's Step 6 describes doFirst, trades, candidates and defense with flat player-id arrays, and carries an inline validator that requires them. The repository's own validate.py says in its docstring that it is the only copy and that the RUNBOOK.md duplicate drifted from it - and it requires the opposite: trades as objects with playerId, name and detail, which is also what the app renders. The two cannot both be satisfied on the same key. I took the repository validator, published the object form, and added theirGain, candidates and defense alongside so nothing the runbook asks for is missing. Both files pass repo validate.py with exit 0; the runbook's inline copy raises TypeError on the object form. Someone should delete the inline duplicate from the runbook, which is the exact failure its own docstring warns about.
